ï»¿    **COMMENTS**
The domain of active strike-slip deformation in NW and W Slovenia is positioned between the S vergent thrust domain in the Friuli area of NE Italy and SW thrusting domain of the Dinarides. Earthquake and geology data in NE Italy indicate that the prevailing mechanism of deformation is thrusting on E-W oriented planes whereas dextral-reverse and purely dextral strike-slip displacements on NNW-SSE oriented planes occur further E and SE. The prevailing fault orientation in the Dinarides is in the orogen-parallel NW-SE direction. Earthquakes and geologic data along these faults exhibit thrust focal mechanisms in the southern and central parts of the Dinarides, and dextral-reverse mechanisms in the northern Dinarides.
The first stage of mountain building connected to the South Alpine orogeny is Eocene thrusting and reverse fault movements along the NE Adriatic margin. During the Eocene to Lower Miocene, NE-SW directed shortening led to thrusting and uplift along SW vergent NW-SE oriented faults in the Central and External Dinarides (e.g. Tari and Pamic, 1998; Pamic et al., 2002), Julian and Friuli Alps, and E Dolomites (Doglioni, 1987). The Eocene Dinaric faults were strongly dismembered by younger, mostly late Oligocene and Miocene, south-vergent South-Alpine thrusts and steep reverse faults, which resulted in overthrusting and refolding of Dinaric structures both in the Friuli region (Doglioni, 1987; Nussbaum, 2000) and in the Julian Alps (Placer and Car, 1998). During Late Oligocene-Miocene South Alpine shortening resulted in formation of E-W oriented thrust and reverse faults. During the Mioceneâ€“Pliocene transition, the Alpine region was subjected to a change in regional style of deformation probably due to termination of subduction and slab pull along the eastern edge of the Carpathians (Horvath and Cloetingh, 1996). This change in the regional stress field coupled with the continuous northward motion of Adria resulted in inversion and reactivation of previous favourably oriented structures. The NW-SE oriented faults were reactivated in a dextral strike-slip manner and continue to exhibit such kinematics with the ongoing deformation of 2mm/yr towards NNE oriented horizontal velocy vectors recorded by GPS measurements (Grenerczy, 2002).
The majority of regional seismicity is concentrated on N and E margins of the Adria and the region of W Julian Alps together with Friuli-Venezia Giulia, represents seismically most active area in the entire Alpine region. The Ravne Fault has hosted moderate sized earthquakes in 1998 and 2004 with magnitude values of 5.7 and 5.2 respectivately, while no previous historical or instrumental recordings placing seismic events on this fault exist. Only 8 km to thesouth, the Idrija Fault, parallel to the Ravne Fault, was the host fault of the M 6.8 1511 earthquake that is the strongest recorded earthquake in the region.
Approximately 30 km to the ESE from this Source lies the source of the 1976 Gemona earthquake that occured on E-W oriented thrust plane.
This Source lies on the NW-SE trending, dextral strike-slip Ravne Fault that runs through the eastern part of the Southern Alps. The surface trace of the Ravne Fault can be observed in the field and on satellite and digital topographic imagery over a distance of approximately 30 km and along its trace exhibits segmented geometry in a form of right stepping segments.
We set the depth interval of this Source based on data of local and regional geologic setting. We heve obtained the average strike and dip of the source on the base of field measurements of the geometrical characteristics of the fault traces (Kastelic et al., 2008) and characteristics obtained on spatial distribution of the latest seismic events and their focal mechanism solutions (Bajc et al., 2001; Kastelic, 2008). Average rake of the source was determined by using measured data on microkinematic indicators present within the fault zone combained with focal mechanism solutions.
Values of minimum and maximum slip rates were based considering measured horizontal velocity vectors obtained from GPS measurements (Grenerczy et al., 2005) and considering geometrical characteristics of the source. Maximum magnitude of the Source was assigned after the April 12th 1998 earthquake, that is strongest earthquake reported for the Ravne Fault.

pictures.c: Regional location of the Idrija and Ravne faults with other major structural elements of NW Slovenia. The Idrija Fault system runs parallel to the Ravne Fault, that lies 8 km to the north and exhibits better rock exposure. To the NW, the fault exhibits a change in strike to WNW-ESE, and interaction with E-W oriented thrusts (after Kastelic [2008]).

pictures.t: Geometry of Ravne Fault with data on (paleo)stress tensor orientation
pictures.c: To obtain constraints on the nature of deformation within the Ravne Fault zone orientations of  stress paleotensors were calculated on the basis of inversion of microkinematic data measured in the field. Results show a general orientation N-S for the maximum stress axis, which is consistent to more regional data obtained from GPS campaigns (after Kastelic [2008]).

pictures.t: Distribution of seismic sequences of 1998 and 2004 along Ravne Fault
pictures.c: Recent seismic activity of the source is testified by earthquake sequences of 1998 and 2004 both occuring at the NW end of the Bovec - Tolminka Springs source. The 1998 event shows a uniform spatial distribution of the sequence in NW-SE direction with dextral strike-slip kinematics, while the 2004 sequence besides the continuation of the NW-SE distribution of the aftershocks and obliqur dextral- thrust kinematics for the main event, exhibits also a group of aftershocks lined in an E-W direction with thrust movements (after Kastelic et al. [2008]).
